The pilot’s loss of control after a rejected takeoff, which resulted in a noseover.
The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane during the takeoff roll.

The pilot’s improper decision to takeoff from an unimproved airstrip with a high density altitude which degraded its climb performance and led to a collision with vegetation off the end of the airstrip.
A loss of engine power due to the use of improper fuel. Contributing to the accident was the failure of the pilot and ground personnel to ensure that the airplane was serviced with the proper fuel.
The pilot receiving instruction’s excessive use of brakes during landing, and the pilot providing instruction’s inadequate supervision, resulting in a nose-over.

The main rotor transmission mount design, which resulted in an in-flight vibration/oscillation, and damage to the helicopter during an emergency descent and hard landing. The ground crew’s failure to remain clear of a tag line during sling load operations, resulting in his entanglement.
A loss of engine power for an undetermined reason.
The pilot’s inadvertent entanglement of a lightweight Kevlar long line into the helicopters operating main rotor system, resulting in a severe imbalance and separation of the main rotor gearbox.
A total loss of engine power for undetermined reasons, which necessitated an emergency hovering autorotation, during which the helicopter impacted trees and terrain.

A fatigue fracture of the governor-to-fuel control Pc line, which resulted in a partial loss of engine power.

The pilot's loss of directional control while landing, which resulted in a runway excursion.
The pilot’s failure to adequately monitor the environment and maintain clearance from the power lines while maneuvering at low altitude.

The pilot’s encounter with severe turbulence at night which resulted in an extended downwind and collision with wires during the base turn.
